docs.text: Webhook-Async Documentation ¶ A standalone Rust webhook receiver and asynchronous job engine. What is webhook-async ? ¶ webhook-async is a modern, memory-safe, standalone executable designed to receive HTTP webhooks and run tasks with complete reliability. It solves the two biggest challenges of traditional webhook infrastructure: 1. Preserving Upstream Compatibility : Full compatibility with adnanh/webhook v2.8.3 hook definitions, trigger rules, HMAC signatures, IP whitelists, and template preprocessing. 2. Eliminating Dropped Webhooks & Timeouts : Provides a durable, transactional queue engine (SQLite, Valkey, Redis) that commits jobs before acknowledging HTTP 202 Accepted , running tasks asynchronously with retries and concurrency limits. Core Features ¶ Single Self-Contained Binary : Written in pure Rust. No Node.js runtime, no Python, no mandatory Docker engine. Dual Execution Engine : Synchronous : Direct process execution returning stdout/stderr immediately; requires zero database or queue storage. Asynchronous : Durable queue committing an immutable execution snapshot before returning HTTP 202. Pluggable Storage Backends : SQLite (default): Embedded, WAL-mode, multi-threaded with busy timeouts. Valkey & Redis : Distributed scale-out using atomic Lua scripts and clustered hash-tagged keys. Integrated Web UI : Lightweight Askama server-rendered templates, HTMX reactive components, and Server-Sent Events (SSE). Hardened Process Execution : Commands run with an explicit argument vector (no shell string interpolation), process group isolation ( -pgid ), execution timeouts, and automatic temporary file cleanup. Dynamic Hot Reloading : Update hook definitions on the fly via SIGHUP , SIGUSR1 , or --hotreload polling with zero downtime. Architecture at a Glance ¶ [ Incoming Webhook / Client ] │ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Axum HTTP Receiver │ │ (Auth, Trigger Rules)│ └───────────┬────────────┘ │ ┌─────────────────┴─────────────────┐ │ Mode Resolution │ ▼ ▼ [ Synchronous Hook ] [ Asynchronous Hook ] │ │ ▼ ▼ ┌──────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────┐ │ Direct Executor │ │ Storage / Queue │ │ (Process Group) │ │ (SQLite / Valkey) │ └─────────┬────────┘ └──────────┬──────────┘ │ │ (HTTP 202) ▼ ▼ Combined Output ┌─────────────────┐ (HTTP 200/500) │ Worker Pool │ │ (Heartbeat, Ack)│ └────────┬────────┘ ▼ [ Direct Executor ] 60-Second Quickstart ¶ 1. Download the Binary ¶ Download the precompiled standalone binary for your architecture from GitHub Releases : # Linux x86_64 example curl -L -o webhook-async https://github.com/sunilsankar/webhook-async/releases/download/v0.1.0-beta/webhook-async-linux-amd64 chmod +x webhook-async sudo mv webhook-async /usr/local/bin/ 2. Define a Minimal Hook ( hooks.json ) ¶ [ { "id": "deploy-app", "execute-command": "/bin/echo", "pass-arguments-to-command": [ { "source": "payload", "name": "ref" }, { "source": "payload", "name": "commit" } ], "response-message": "Deployment initiated.", "include-command-output-in-response": true } ] 3. Run the Server ¶ webhook-async server --port 9000 --hooks hooks.json 4. Trigger the Webhook ¶ curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/hooks/deploy-app \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"ref": "refs/heads/main", "commit": "05dc3f3"}' Response: refs/heads/main 05dc3f3 Documentation Navigation ¶ Deployment Guide : Step-by-step guides for Linux (systemd), Docker Compose, Kubernetes, macOS (launchd), Windows, and Reverse Proxies (Caddy/Nginx). Configuration Reference : Complete schema for config.toml , hook definitions, trigger rules, parameter extraction, and template preprocessing. API Reference : Complete documentation for receiver endpoints, health checks, administrative REST API ( /api/v1/* ), and SSE real-time stream. Operations & Backups : Signal handling, zero-downtime hot reload, non-blocking SQLite hot backups ( VACUUM INTO ), logging, and disaster recovery. docs.text: API Reference & Usage ¶ ← Back to Home • Deployment Guide • Configuration Reference • Operations 1. Authentication & Security ¶ All administrative and operational endpoints under /api/v1 are secured with Bearer token authentication. Authentication Header ¶ Authorization: Bearer <WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN> Fail-Secure Default : If [auth].admin_token_env or [auth].admin_token_file is not configured, admin endpoints return 503 Service Unavailable with message "Admin token not configured." . Constant-Time Verification : Uses subtle::ConstantTimeEq to prevent timing side-channel attacks. Built-in Rate Limiting : 60 requests per minute per token. Breaching the rate limit returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After: 60 header. 2. Webhook Receiver Endpoints ¶ 1. Root Liveness & Ping ¶ GET / Returns 200 OK with body "OK" . Used by upstream load balancers and network checks. 2. Trigger a Webhook ¶ POST /{url_prefix}/{hook_id} Processes an incoming webhook. Supports sub-paths if the hook ID contains slashes (e.g. github/deploy ). Response Status Codes ¶ 200 OK : Synchronous hook executed successfully. Body contains command output (if configured) or response-message . 202 Accepted : Asynchronous hook accepted and durably committed to queue. Body contains job_id , status: "queued" , and message . 400 Bad Request : Trigger rules were not satisfied (or custom status code). 405 Method Not Allowed : Request HTTP method not permitted by hook. 413 Payload Too Large : Request body exceeds server.max_body_bytes . 429 Too Many Requests : Queue capacity full ( queue.max_pending_jobs reached). 500 Internal Server Error : Rule evaluation error or synchronous command execution failure. 503 Service Unavailable : Storage backend unavailable; asynchronous hook was not acknowledged. 3. System Health & OpenAPI Endpoints ¶ 1. Basic Health Check ¶ GET /api/v1/health (No authentication required) Response: { "status": "ok", "version": "0.1.0" } 2. Storage Readiness Probe ¶ GET /api/v1/ready (No authentication required) Performs a live storage ping ( SELECT 1 or Redis PING ). Response: { "status": "ready", "storage": "connected" } Returns 503 Service Unavailable if the storage backend is unreachable. 3. OpenAPI 3.1 Specification ¶ GET /api/v1/openapi.json (No authentication required) Returns the complete OpenAPI 3.1 schema documenting all schemas, endpoints, and error types. 4. Administrative REST Endpoints ¶ (Requires Authorization: Bearer <token> ) 1. Queue Statistics ¶ GET /api/v1/stats Returns job counts across all 8 canonical states. Response: { "counts_by_state": { "queued": 0, "running": 2, "retry_wait": 0, "succeeded": 1420, "failed": 3, "cancel_requested": 0, "cancelled": 1, "dead_letter": 0 }, "pending_count": 2 } 2. List & Filter Jobs ¶ GET /api/v1/jobs?state={state}&hook_id={hook_id}&limit={limit}&offset={offset} Query Parameters ¶ state : Optional filter by state ( queued , running , retry_wait , succeeded , failed , cancel_requested , cancelled , dead_letter ). hook_id : Optional filter by hook identifier. limit : Number of items per page (1 to 500, default 50). offset : Pagination offset (default 0). Response: { "items": [ { "id": "8a01cb6b-4e12-4f10-9c41-89e70197da96", "hook_id": "deploy-app", "state": "succeeded", "priority": 0, "created_at": "2026-11-13T10:15:30.123456789Z", "started_at": "2026-11-13T10:15:30.130000000Z", "completed_at": "2026-11-13T10:15:34.250000000Z", "attempt": 1, "max_attempts": 5, "exit_code": 0, "stdout_preview": "Deploy successful.", "stderr_preview": "" } ], "total": 1426, "limit": 50, "offset": 0 } 3. Get Job Details & Attempts ¶ GET /api/v1/jobs/{id} Returns the full job record and complete execution attempt history. 4. Retry a Job ¶ POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/retry Transitions a failed or dead_letter job back to queued . Increments max_attempts if necessary to allow execution. Response: { "job": { "id": "8a01cb6b-4e12-4f10-9c41-89e70197da96", "state": "queued", "attempt": 2, "max_attempts": 6 } } Returns 409 Conflict if the job is not in a retryable state. 5. Cancel a Job ¶ POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel Cancels a queued , retry_wait , or running job. If running, the worker's heartbeat loop sends SIGKILL to the child process group. Response: { "job": { "id": "8a01cb6b-4e12-4f10-9c41-89e70197da96", "state": "cancel_requested" } } 6. List Active Hooks ¶ GET /api/v1/hooks Returns metadata for all loaded hooks. All secrets and sensitive parameters are masked or redacted. 7. List Active Workers ¶ GET /api/v1/workers Returns all registered worker nodes, concurrency settings, active tasks, and heartbeats. 8. Storage Status ¶ GET /api/v1/storage/status Returns backend kind ( sqlite , valkey , redis ), storage capabilities, and live connectivity status. 9. Real-Time Server-Sent Events (SSE) ¶ GET /api/v1/events Pushes live queue statistics updates every 2 seconds over a persistent HTTP stream. 5. Complete Curl Recipe Book ¶ Triggering Hooks ¶ Asynchronous Webhook with Idempotency Key ¶ curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/hooks/deploy-app \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: github-delivery-1029384" \ -d '{"ref": "refs/heads/main", "commit": "05dc3f3"}' Synchronous Webhook ¶ curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/hooks/sync-task \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"action": "ping"}' Administrative Management ¶ Set your token variable: export TOKEN="your-admin-token-here" Check System Health ¶ curl -s http://localhost:9000/api/v1/health curl -s http://localhost:9000/api/v1/ready View Live Queue Statistics ¶ curl -s http://localhost:9000/api/v1/stats \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq . List Dead-Lettered Jobs ¶ curl -s "http://localhost:9000/api/v1/jobs?state=dead_letter&limit=20" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq . View Specific Job & Execution Logs ¶ curl -s http://localhost:9000/api/v1/jobs/8a01cb6b-4e12-4f10-9c41-89e70197da96 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq . Retry a Dead-Lettered Job ¶ curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/api/v1/jobs/8a01cb6b-4e12-4f10-9c41-89e70197da96/retry \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq . Cancel an In-Flight Job ¶ curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/api/v1/jobs/8a01cb6b-4e12-4f10-9c41-89e70197da96/cancel \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq . Stream Live Queue Metrics (SSE) ¶ curl -N http://localhost:9000/api/v1/events \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

docs.text: Configuration Reference ¶ ← Back to Home • Deployment Guide • API Reference • Operations 1. Application Configuration ( config.toml ) ¶ webhook-async uses a single TOML file for server and system configuration. [server] host = "0.0.0.0" # Bind address port = 9000 # Bind port url_prefix = "hooks" # Route prefix (e.g. /hooks/{id}) max_body_bytes = 10485760 # Maximum request body size (10 MB) max_multipart_mem_bytes = 1048576 # Memory buffer limit for multipart parts (1 MB) hook_files = ["/etc/webhook/hooks.json"]# Paths to hook definition files hot_reload = true # Automatically reload hook files on change default_http_methods = ["POST"] # Fallback methods when hook omits http-methods response_headers = [ # Global response headers added to all replies { name = "X-Service", value = "webhook-async" }, { name = "Access-Control-Allow-Origin", value = "*" } ] use_x_request_id = true # Propagate or generate X-Request-Id header x_request_id_limit = 64 # Maximum character length for X-Request-Id trust_proxy_headers = true # Honor X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP for remote-addr [storage] backend = "sqlite" # Storage engine: "sqlite", "valkey", or "redis" [storage.sqlite] database_url = "sqlite:///var/lib/webhook-async/data.db?mode=rwc" wal_mode = true # Enable Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) for concurrency busy_timeout_ms = 5000 # Maximum wait time on busy database locks # Valkey / Redis configuration (uncomment when backend is "valkey" or "redis"): # [storage.valkey] # url = "redis://10.0.1.50:6379/0" # Accepts redis://, rediss://, valkey://, valkeys:// # key_prefix = "webhook_async:" # Namespaced key prefix (uses hash-tags for cluster) [worker] concurrency = 8 # Maximum concurrent background tasks poll_interval_ms = 250 # Delay between queue poll attempts when idle lease_duration_seconds = 60 # Lease window granted to worker for each claim heartbeat_interval_seconds = 15 # Frequency at which active worker extends lease shutdown_grace_seconds = 30 # Maximum drain duration on shutdown signal [queue] max_pending_jobs = 10000 # Maximum queued jobs (returns HTTP 429 when full) default_max_attempts = 5 # Maximum execution attempts before dead-lettering retry_base_delay_seconds = 5 # Exponential backoff base delay retry_max_delay_seconds = 300 # Exponential backoff ceiling delay default_timeout_seconds = 300 # Maximum execution time per command attempt max_output_bytes = 65536 # Maximum stdout/stderr output captured (64 KB) idempotency_retention_seconds = 86400 # Idempotency deduplication TTL (24 hours) [ui] enabled = true # Enable built-in Web management UI bind = "127.0.0.1:9001" # Dedicated bind for the Web UI path_prefix = "" # Optional URL subpath prefix (e.g. "/admin") [auth] admin_token_env = "WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN" # Environment variable containing admin Bearer token # admin_token_file = "/run/secrets/admin_token" # Or file path containing admin token 2. Hook Definitions ( hooks.json / hooks.yaml ) ¶ Hooks can be configured in either JSON or YAML. Complete Hook Schema ¶ [ { "id": "github-webhook", "execute-command": "/opt/scripts/deploy.sh", "command-working-directory": "/opt/repo", "response-message": "Deployment initiated.", "response-headers": [ { "name": "X-Custom-Header", "value": "webhook-processed" } ], "include-command-output-in-response": false, "include-command-output-in-response-on-error": true, "http-methods": ["POST"], "success-http-response-code": 200, "trigger-rule-mismatch-http-response-code": 400, "trigger-signature-soft-failures": false, "incoming-payload-content-type": "application/json", "async": true, "trigger-rule": { "and": [ { "match": { "type": "payload-hmac-sha256", "secret": "{{ getenv \"GITHUB_SECRET\" }}", "parameter": { "source": "header", "name": "X-Hub-Signature-256" } } }, { "match": { "type": "value", "value": "refs/heads/main", "parameter": { "source": "payload", "name": "ref" } } } ] }, "pass-arguments-to-command": [ { "source": "payload", "name": "head_commit.id" }, { "source": "payload", "name": "pusher.name" }, { "source": "request", "name": "remote-addr" } ], "pass-environment-to-command": [ { "source": "payload", "name": "repository.name", "envname": "REPO_NAME" }, { "source": "header", "name": "X-GitHub-Delivery", "envname": "DELIVERY_ID" } ], "pass-file-to-command": [ { "source": "entire-payload", "envname": "PAYLOAD_FILE" } ], "parse-parameters-as-json": [ { "source": "payload", "name": "custom_data" } ] } ] 3. Parameter Extraction ( source ) ¶ Parameters can be extracted and mapped to command arguments, environment variables, files, or trigger rule checks. Source Description Example header Canonical MIME HTTP request header. {"source": "header", "name": "X-GitHub-Event"} url / query URL query parameter. {"source": "url", "name": "branch"} payload Body value from JSON, XML, or Form payload. Supports dot notation. {"source": "payload", "name": "commit.author.email"} raw-request-body The unparsed UTF-8 body string. {"source": "raw-request-body"} request Request metadata ( remote-addr , method ). {"source": "request", "name": "remote-addr"} string Static literal string. {"source": "string", "name": "production"} entire-payload Full raw body written to temporary file ( pass-file-to-command ). {"source": "entire-payload", "envname": "BODY_FILE"} entire-headers JSON map of all headers. {"source": "entire-headers", "envname": "HEADERS_JSON"} entire-query JSON map of all query parameters. {"source": "entire-query", "envname": "QUERY_JSON"} 4. Trigger Rules ( trigger-rule ) ¶ Trigger rules determine whether the webhook is allowed to run. Rule Combinators ¶ and : Array of rules; all must evaluate to true . or : Array of rules; passes if any rule evaluates to true . not : Inverts the result of a child rule. Matcher Types ( type ) ¶ 1. value (String Equality) ¶ Constant-time equality comparison: { "match": { "type": "value", "value": "refs/heads/main", "parameter": { "source": "payload", "name": "ref" } } } 2. regex (Pattern Match) ¶ Matches value against a regular expression: { "match": { "type": "regex", "regex": "^v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$", "parameter": { "source": "payload", "name": "ref" } } } 3. payload-hmac-sha1 , payload-hmac-sha256 , payload-hmac-sha512 ¶ Constant-time HMAC hex verification with secret: { "match": { "type": "payload-hmac-sha256", "secret": "{{ getenv \"WEBHOOK_SECRET\" }}", "parameter": { "source": "header", "name": "X-Hub-Signature-256" } } } Supports optional prefix format (e.g. sha256=abcdef... ) and comma-separated multiple signatures. 4. ip-whitelist ¶ Verifies client IP against whitespace-delimited IPs or CIDR blocks: { "match": { "type": "ip-whitelist", "ip-whitelist": "192.168.1.0/24 10.0.0.1 2001:db8::/32" } } 5. scalr-signature ¶ Validates Scalr-compliant HMAC-SHA1 timestamp and signature: { "match": { "type": "scalr-signature", "secret": "{{ getenv \"SCALR_KEY\" }}" } } 5. Execution Mode Precedence ¶ Execution mode is resolved using this strict precedence hierarchy: ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ Is hook "async" specified? │ └───────────────┬───────────────┘ │ ┌────────────────┴────────────────┐ ▼ YES ▼ NO ┌───────────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ Use hook.async value │ │ CLI flag --async / --sync? │ │ (true/false) │ └───────────────┬───────────────┘ └───────────────────────┘ │ ┌────────────────┴────────────────┐ ▼ Set ▼ None ┌─────────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────────┐ │ Use CLI flag mode │ │ Default: SYNCHRONOUS │ └─────────────────────┘ └───────────────────────┘ 6. Template Preprocessing ( --template ) ¶ Start the server or validation with --template to enable dynamic configuration preprocessing: {{ getenv "VAR_NAME" "fallback" }} : Injects environment variable with optional default. {{ cat "/path/to/file" }} : Reads file content and trims trailing newline. {{ credential "secret_name" }} : Reads systemd $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY file with fallback to env var. {{ ... | js }} : Encodes value as a safe JSON string literal.

docs.text: Operations & Runbook ¶ ← Back to Home • Deployment Guide • Configuration Reference • API Reference 1. Process Lifecycle & Signal Handling ¶ webhook-async handles standard POSIX signals for lifecycle events: Signal Action Behavior SIGHUP Reload Hooks Re-reads and re-validates hook definition files. Current active hooks remain untouched if parsing or validation fails. SIGUSR1 Reload Hooks Upstream-compatible reload signal. SIGTERM Graceful Shutdown Stops accepting new HTTP requests, drains workers for shutdown_grace_seconds , and cleanly unlinks PID/socket files. SIGINT Graceful Shutdown Intercepts Ctrl+C for clean termination. Sending Reload Signals ¶ # Using kill with PID file kill -HUP $(cat /var/run/webhook-async.pid) # Using systemd sudo systemctl reload webhook-async 2. Dynamic Hot Reloading ¶ When --hotreload is specified (or server.hot_reload = true in config.toml ), webhook-async polls the configured hook files for modifications every 2.5 seconds. Invariant Guarantees ¶ Atomic Swap : The internal routing table is updated atomically using a thread-safe read-write lock ( Arc<RwLock<...>> ). Immutable Job Snapshots : In-flight and queued jobs retain the exact ExecutionSpec snapshot captured when they were accepted. Reloading hooks never mutates running tasks. Fail-Safe : If a modified hook file contains invalid syntax or unknown fields, an error is logged and the server continues running with the previous valid configuration. 3. Zero-Downtime SQLite Hot Backups ¶ Because webhook-async uses SQLite in WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode with multi-connection concurrency and busy timeouts, backups can be taken while the server is accepting requests without table locks. Online Backup Command ¶ sqlite3 /var/lib/webhook-async/data.db "VACUUM INTO '/var/backups/webhook-async-$(date +%F-%H%M).db'" Automated Nightly Backup Cron Script ¶ Create /etc/cron.daily/webhook-async-backup : #!/bin/bash set -euo pipefail BACKUP_DIR="/var/backups/webhook-async" DB_PATH="/var/lib/webhook-async/data.db" TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S) mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR" # Perform online atomic backup sqlite3 "$DB_PATH" "VACUUM INTO '$BACKUP_DIR/backup-$TIMESTAMP.db'" # Retain backups for 14 days find "$BACKUP_DIR" -type f -name "backup-*.db" -mtime +14 -delete Make executable: sudo chmod +x /etc/cron.daily/webhook-async-backup Restoring from Backup ¶ Stop the service: bash sudo systemctl stop webhook-async Replace the database: bash sudo cp /var/backups/webhook-async/backup-20261113_020000.db /var/lib/webhook-async/data.db sudo rm -f /var/lib/webhook-async/data.db-wal /var/lib/webhook-async/data.db-shm sudo chown webhook:webhook /var/lib/webhook-async/data.db Start the service: bash sudo systemctl start webhook-async 4. Valkey / Redis Persistence & Backups ¶ For distributed deployments using Valkey or Redis: Persistence Requirements ¶ Always enable Append-Only File (AOF) in valkey.conf / redis.conf : text appendonly yes appendfsync everysec Configure RDB snapshots: text save 900 1 save 300 10 save 60 10000 Triggering Manual Backup ¶ # Trigger background RDB snapshot valkey-cli bgsave # Copy the generated dump.rdb cp /var/lib/valkey/dump.rdb /var/backups/valkey-dump-$(date +%F).rdb 5. Logging, Diagnostics & Crash Safety ¶ Structured Logging ¶ Configure logging outputs: - Standard output: --verbose or --debug . - Dedicated log file: --logfile /var/log/webhook-async/service.log . Panic Immunity ( --nopanic ) ¶ In production, pass --nopanic (or -nopanic ). This installs a custom panic hook that logs the stack trace without aborting the server process, preventing individual malformed requests from causing an outage. Storage Health Inspection via CLI ¶ webhook-async storage status --config /etc/webhook-async/config.toml Output: Storage Backend: SQLite (Embedded) Capabilities: Priority Ordering: true Multi-Host Shared: false Idempotency TTL: true Connectivity: Connected Counts: Queued: 0 Running: 2 Succeeded: 1420 Failed: 3 Dead Letter: 0 Total Pending: 2

docs.text: Security Architecture & Hardening ¶ ← Back to Home • Deployment Guide • Configuration Reference • API Reference 1. Threat Model & Principles ¶ webhook-async receives untrusted payloads from the public Internet and executes administrative commands on internal infrastructure. Security is the paramount operational constraint. Foundational Principles ¶ Memory Safety : Written entirely in 100% safe Rust. No buffer overflows, use-after-free, or data races. Fail-Secure Defaults : Administrative endpoints require explicit token configuration. If unconfigured, access is rejected with 503 Service Unavailable . Zero Shell Interpolation : Commands are executed directly via OS system calls ( execve ) with discrete argument vectors. Payload strings are never evaluated by a shell interpreter. Constant-Time Verification : All cryptographic signatures and authentication tokens are validated in constant time to prevent timing side-channel attacks. Process Sandboxing : Command executions are assigned discrete process groups ( -pgid ), bounded by strict execution timeouts, and killed with SIGKILL on timeout or cancellation. 2. Process Execution Security ¶ Direct Process Execution vs Shell Injection ¶ Vulnerable systems often run webhook commands like this: # VULNERABLE: sh -c "deploy.sh --branch $BRANCH" # Payload: "; rm -rf / ;" In webhook-async , commands are invoked directly: let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&spec.executable); cmd.args(&spec.args); cmd.envs(&spec.env); Payload contents can only occupy designated discrete argument elements or environment variables. It is mathematically impossible for a payload value to inject additional command flags or shell operators. Process Group Sandboxing ¶ Child processes are launched in their own process group ( process_group(0) ). If execution exceeds queue.default_timeout_seconds or an operator cancels the task, webhook-async sends SIGKILL to -pgid . This guarantees that background subprocesses, sub-shells, or detached child processes are terminated immediately rather than orphaned. 3. Cryptographic Verification & Signatures ¶ Public webhooks should always enforce cryptographic signature verification using provider secrets. Supported HMAC verification matchers: - payload-hmac-sha256 (GitHub X-Hub-Signature-256 , Stripe) - payload-hmac-sha1 (GitHub legacy X-Hub-Signature , Bitbucket) - payload-hmac-sha512 - scalr-signature (HMAC-SHA1 Date + Body verification) Constant-Time Implementation ¶ All HMAC digests and tokens are verified using subtle::ConstantTimeEq : mac.verify_slice(&candidate_mac).map_err(...) Timing attacks attempting to deduce secrets byte-by-byte are mathematically defeated. 4. Web Management UI Security ¶ Session Tokens : Login issues a cryptographically random UUID session token stored in an HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax cookie. CSRF Tokens : Every mutation (Retry, Cancel, Logout) strictly requires a matching X-CSRF-Token header or form field. Strict HTML Escaping : Askama templates strictly escape all user-supplied variables by default, defeating Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Isolated Binding : The management UI can be bound to a separate IP/port (e.g. 127.0.0.1:9001 ) away from the public webhook receiver. 5. Security Checklist ¶ [ ] Run webhook-async as an unprivileged dedicated service account ( webhook ). [ ] Set WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN with at least 32 cryptographically random characters. [ ] Enforce HMAC signature validation on all public hooks. [ ] Bound execution timeouts ( queue.default_timeout_seconds ). [ ] Use direct TLS ( --secure ) or an authenticated reverse proxy (Nginx/Caddy) with HTTPS.

docs.text: Troubleshooting Matrix ¶ ← Back to Home • Deployment Guide • Configuration Reference • API Reference HTTP Status Codes & Solutions ¶ Status Cause Resolution 400 Hook rules were not satisfied. Trigger rule mismatch (e.g. invalid HMAC secret, missing header, payload branch mismatch). Run server with --verbose to inspect trigger evaluation logs. Verify HMAC secret matches provider. 405 Method Not Allowed Webhook sent with an HTTP method not listed in hook's http-methods . Update hook's http-methods array or send the request using POST . 413 Payload Too Large Request payload exceeds server.max_body_bytes . Increase server.max_body_bytes in config.toml (default is 10 MB). 429 Queue capacity full In-flight queued jobs have reached queue.max_pending_jobs . Increase worker concurrency ( worker.concurrency ), add dedicated worker nodes, or increase queue.max_pending_jobs . 429 Rate limit exceeded Exceeded 60 requests/minute on administrative endpoints. Wait for the duration in Retry-After: 60 or throttle management scripts. 500 Internal Server Error Synchronous command returned non-zero exit code or rule evaluation threw an unhandled error. Inspect stdout/stderr in response (if include-command-output-in-response-on-error: true ) or inspect server logs. 503 Service Unavailable (On Hook Post) Storage backend is unreachable when accepting an asynchronous webhook. Check SQLite filesystem permissions or verify Valkey/Redis network connectivity. Webhook was not acknowledged. 503 Admin token not configured Calling /api/v1/* without configuring admin_token_env or admin_token_file . Set WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN in the environment or set admin_token_file in config.toml . Worker & Execution Issues ¶ Job Transitions Immediately to dead_letter ¶ Cause : Executable path or working directory does not exist or lacks execute permissions. Why : webhook-async classifies missing binaries as non-transient Configuration errors and dead-letters immediately to prevent infinite retry loops. Solution : Use absolute executable paths (e.g. /usr/local/bin/deploy.sh ) and ensure the webhook user has read and execute permissions. Worker Heartbeat / Lease Expiry ¶ Symptom : Job stays in running and is reclaimed by another worker after 60s. Cause : Task process completely locked up the CPU or network, preventing the asynchronous heartbeat loop from renewing the lease. Solution : Ensure system resources are sufficient, or increase worker.lease_duration_seconds (e.g. to 120s). database is locked on SQLite ¶ Cause : High concurrency without Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) or missing busy timeout. Solution : Verify that wal_mode = true and busy_timeout_ms = 5000 are configured in [storage.sqlite] . Diagnostic Commands ¶ Validate Configuration Files ¶ webhook-async config validate --config config.toml --hooks hooks.json Check Storage Health ¶ webhook-async storage status --config config.toml Test Webhook Triggers Locally ¶ curl -v -X POST http://localhost:9000/hooks/test-hook \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"test": true}'
